what_players_say_it_is: Players describe AION 2 as a visually impressive Korean MMORPG with enjoyable flying, character customization, satisfying early combat, and a long progression grind. However, several reviewers feel that the endgame becomes a repetitive gear-grinding treadmill dominated by RNG, restrictive subscriptions, aggressive monetization, and pay-to-win concerns.

aspects.evidence: Players praise flying, exploration, early combat, character progression, and satisfying skill combinations. Others describe repetitive grinding, tedious solo dungeons, excessive stat systems, and combat that becomes boring when optimized with macros.

Players repeatedly describe the world as beautiful, visually stunning, and polished. Character customization is also praised, although some reviewers consider the game generic or soulless despite its appearance.
The provided reviews do not explicitly evaluate the soundtrack, sound effects, or voice acting.

One player describes the opening story and introductory quests positively, including the way early quest sequences are separated from other players. The reviews provide little evidence about the quality of the broader narrative.
One player reports generally acceptable performance on an older laptop, with occasional possible lag or loading issues during teleportation. Another reports poor ping from the OCE region.

A player reports account-linking problems that can result in lost characters, purchases, and progress if the wrong workaround is used. A conflicting F12 key binding also caused the interface to disappear, although the player found a workaround.

Players criticize the monthly subscription required for marketplace access and important convenience benefits. Some feel free-to-play progression is possible but significantly slower, while others believe the game's systems push players toward spending.

Players discuss faction PvP, group dungeons, raids, and the desire to play with friends. Some appreciate equalized or power-restricted PvP modes, while server restrictions and account progression can complicate playing together.

Players enjoy the early quests, flying, character creation, mounts, dungeons, and raids. However, reviewers criticize gear-score gates, repetitive endgame progression, and the limited appeal of continuing for months.

Players describe basic class combat as relatively simple and accessible, while higher-level dungeons and raids demand more mechanical knowledge. Others find progression excessively difficult because crafting can fail and destroy valuable materials.

Players praise flying and its integration into exploration, and one reviewer appreciates being able to switch between two combat and movement-control styles. Another criticizes movement as floaty, while a key-binding conflict caused interface confusion.

Players report that developers acknowledged the account-linking problem and were investigating it. However, reviewers remain concerned about account policies, server-transfer restrictions, and systems they consider unfair.

Players criticize the subscription-gated marketplace, premium-currency exchange, progression advantages, and monetization pressure. Some describe the game as pay-to-win, while others accept the model provided they can progress slowly without spending.

pros: Visually impressive world and attractive character designs.
Excellent character customization with many appearance options.
Flying and gliding are enjoyable and integrated into exploration and combat.
Early-game quests and progression can be engaging.
Combat is accessible, with classes that allow players to choose based on aesthetics.
Collecting mounts and earning permanent stats through activities gives players long-term goals.
PvP modes can limit power differences between players.
Free-to-play play is possible without an active subscription.
Players can obtain premium currency through the in-game market.
The game offers group dungeons, raids, exploration, and character progression.
cons: Monthly subscription restricts marketplace access and provides important progression and convenience benefits.
Endgame progression relies heavily on gear-score requirements, resource grinding, and RNG.
Crafting can fail and consume valuable materials despite substantial time investment.
Energy restrictions and slow recharge limit dungeon farming.
Market manipulation and scalping can inflate crafting costs.
Combat can become repetitive when players rely on macros.
Some solo dungeons feel tedious, and movement can feel floaty.
A long-term inactive-account policy reportedly allows character deletion after six months.
Account-linking problems and server-transfer restrictions can threaten progress or complicate playing with friends.
Some players consider the overall design generic or lacking personality.
recommended_for: Players who enjoy Korean MMORPGs and long-term character progression.
Gamers who like collecting equipment, mounts, cosmetics, and permanent stat bonuses.
Players who value detailed character customization and attractive visuals.
Fans of flying-based exploration and fantasy worlds.
Players who enjoy PvE dungeons and challenging endgame raids.
Gamers comfortable with repetitive grinding and RNG-based equipment progression.
Players willing to pay for a subscription or accept slower free-to-play progression.
not_recommended_for: Players who want a completely fair progression system without spending advantages.
Gamers who dislike monthly subscriptions and marketplace restrictions.
Players who find equipment gambling and losing crafting materials frustrating.
Those who prefer meaningful combat decisions over repetitive grinding or macros.
Players who want quick, predictable progression without gear-score gates.
Gamers who cannot commit to regular play but are concerned about inactive-account policies.
Players who expect unrestricted server transfers and easy access to friends on other servers.
gap_vs_developer_description: The developer presents AION 2 as a large-scale MMORPG focused on aerial warfare, faction conflict, and a world built with Unreal Engine 5. Players support the emphasis on attractive visuals, flying, and the fantasy of being a winged Daeva. However, their reviews devote much more attention to character progression, PvE grinding, equipment RNG, subscription restrictions, marketplace access, and monetization. Faction warfare is not the dominant theme in the available player accounts; several reviewers instead describe a largely PvE-focused game with optional or restricted PvP. The biggest gap is between the appealing fantasy and the long-term systems: some players find a rewarding MMO marathon, while others see an expensive, repetitive progression treadmill.
